summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue up ~28% YoY and FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR203.4 crore, but FY26 reported PAT still a loss of INR12.5 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 28% YoY and total income reached INR1,758.8 crore (up 27.8%), with EBITDA of INR57.5 crore (margin about 3.3%) and a loss of INR5 crore versus INR13.7 crore loss a year earlier. FY26 total income was INR6,401.1 crore (up 15.1%) and reported EBITDA INR203.4 crore (margin 3.2%), while PAT was a loss of INR12.5 crore against INR10.5 crore loss in FY25. Management said the FY26 revenue and EBITDA were hit by acquisition costs, a cess provision and the new labour code impact, and it apologised for an error in the April 17, 2026 business update that misstated Q4 growth figures. Management guides FY27 to high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 4.8-5%, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 8,090 units (up 20%), income INR654 crore (up 18%). FY26 volumes 32,572 units (up 9%), income INR2,551 crore (up 9%). Management cited entry-level supply shortages and OEM supply constraints in Keralam.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 1,80,989 units (down 14%), income INR154 crore (up 2%). FY26 service income INR607 crore (down 2%) with volumes 7,39,794 (down 12%); ASP growth offset the volume decline.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 3,716 units (up 59%), income INR645 crore (up 46%). FY26 volumes 12,546 units (up 30%), income INR2,125 crore (up 32%); BharatBenz Punjab acquisition contributed.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 52,443 units (up 13%), income INR97 crore (up 75%). FY26 volumes 2,02,647 (up 10%), income INR351 crore (up 28%).

segments.name: EV (Ather 2-wheelers) new and services
segments.commentary: Q4 new vehicles 3,079 units (up 138%), income INR50 crore (up 113%); service volumes 11,261 (up 81%), income about INR3 crore. FY26 new vehicles 8,154 units (up 89%), income INR137 crore (up 72%); service volumes 39,659 (up 79%), income about INR9 crore (up 18%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin moving to about 4.8-5%; PAT approaching FY24 levels.
Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 FY27 still expected to be loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints.
PV service volumes guided to grow at least 10-12% in FY27, with ASP growth of about 12-13%; CV service volumes guided up 7-8% with ASP up 8-10%.
Standalone sales margin guided at about 3-4% in FY27; spare parts margin guided back to 5.5-6% with revenue growth of 6-8% (ex-BKT).
JLR volume guidance of 550-600 vehicles in FY27 after about 380 Audi/JLR volume shortfall in FY26 (guided about 450); Audi expected to break even this year.
Non-Keralam revenue share to exceed 50% in FY27 from about 47% in FY26; no high-value acquisitions planned in FY27, focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
Inventory to be held at or below 30 days for passenger cars; debt increase attributed to acquisitions, with ~INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.
capex_capacity: Three acquisitions in FY26: BharatBenz dealership in Punjab, Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana, and Audi dealership operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Honda and Piaggio businesses divested (volumes counted to August 2025).
JLR Nagpur operations commenced April 1, 2026; new Maruti touchpoints and multiple Ather touchpoints opened in Q4.
Bank loan facilities increased from INR468 crore to INR643 crore; CRISIL A/Stable rating extended to March 2027.
Management said capex spends will be more monitored and no additional debt is planned beyond what is needed to run the current business.
Acquired Audi and Telangana assets totalled about INR85-90 crore of equipment and showroom assets, with acquisition cost approximately equal.
demand_pricing: Management said demand improved in H2 FY26 after GST reforms in September 2025, with stronger footfall, conversion and entry-level recovery; discounting moderated.
Shortages of entry-level vehicles in Jan-Mar 2026 eased in April-May; Baleno and Fronx have waiting periods.
Post OEM price increases, management reported no noticeable change in demand so far; some pre-ponement of bookings was seen.
Luxury segment: Q4 delayed by UK FTA price-cut expectation; price cuts applied to Range Rover SP and Autobiography, with bookings rising from April.
Service volume: running repair fell about 17-18% as the company deprioritised low-value jobs; collision repair volumes flat; free service volumes recovered in last 6 months.
Maruti share of service volumes about 65-70%; Maruti service volume decline narrowed from -7% (to Q3) to -2% in Q4.
Overall Maruti ASP up about 13% YoY; PV new vehicle weighted ASP up to about 6.5% from about 5.5% three years earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did service volumes fall and what service volume and ASP growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 service volumes fell about 6% and ASP rose about 14%, with revenue up over 8%. For FY27 it guided 10-12% PV service volume growth and matching ASP growth; CV service volume growth of 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the service EBITDA margin gap versus peers close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated margin will not reach 18% because of CV and Ather mix, but the Passenger Car business should reach 18-19% service margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone margins move from about 3% to 5% consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin drag to acquisitions and Telangana expansion; growth is to come from PV service volumes and ASP, plus JLR and Audi ramp-up, with consolidated EBITDA guided to 4.8-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add acquisitions and how will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: No high-value acquisitions planned in FY27. About INR520 crore of the INR600+ crore debt is inventory-linked; term loans will be repaid on schedule, and debt will fall if inventory release generates free cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory under control and what is the demand reaction to OEM price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 49 to 36 (FY25 to FY26); management aims to keep it below 30 days. Post price hikes, demand was flat and supply has normalised in April-May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn sustainably profitable and what happened in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27. Q1 remains affected by Maruti and JLR supply constraints; service volumes expected to grow Q1 over Q1.

risks_watch: Reported FY26 PAT loss of INR12.5 crore; Telangana loss of about INR26-27 crore and cess provision weigh on profitability, with Ind AS depreciation on acquisitions.
Debt rose after acquisitions; management says inventory debt is about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore total, with inventory days to stay below 30.
Error in April 17, 2026 business update, which misstated Q4 revenue growth; management apologised and promised process fixes.
CEO Raj Narayan has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the industry; successor not named on this call.
JLR cyber-attack and supply constraints cost about INR70 crore of top line and INR8-9 crore of bottom line in FY26; Q1 FY27 supply still constrained.
Service volumes in running repair down 17-18%; management needs to show Q1 FY27 volume growth.
Fuel price and geopolitical uncertainty (referred to as a war situation) flagged as demand risks.
key_quotes: Before moving to the business performance, I would like to sincerely apologize for the error in the business update published on April 17 , 2026, for the quarter and the year ended March 31 , 2026, and take this opportunity to clarify the same.
Post the price increase announcement by the OEMs, we have not seen much of a change actually.
In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.
Out of the INR600 odd crores, around INR520 crores is related to the debt on inventory.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand recovery post GST reforms, FY27 guidance and the Q2 FY27 profitability timeline. Cautious and defensive on standalone margins, acquisition losses (Telangana, Audi), debt levels and the April 17 business update error, which management apologised for repeatedly. Evasive on successor CEO and on exact Q1 FY27 profitability, which it framed only as loss-making.
